headline: Medium risk: OpenBBTerminal’s MCP/API surfaces can amplify cross-agent leakage and action confusion when paired with LlamaFactory, while prompt-injection risk is limited by LlamaFactory’s lack of I/O.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LlamaFactory has no filesystem, clipboard, stdin/stdout, browser, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest OpenBBTerminal output by default. OpenBBTerminal does expose MCP/REST/FastAPI surfaces, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel. Any injection path would require unusual manual bridging or external orchestration.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies OpenBBTerminal output into LlamaFactory prompts, injection becomes plausible.
IF an external orchestrator connects OpenBBTerminal MCP output to LlamaFactory input, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate terminals and avoid copy-paste between them.
Disable or firewall OpenBBTerminal MCP/REST endpoints when not needed.
Use a human review step before any OpenBBTerminal output is reused as instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any bridged content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data and can serve it through APIs/MCP, while LlamaFactory is a training/fine-tuning tool with no declared data classes. There is no shared filesystem in the profiles, but OpenBBTerminal’s API surfaces create a plausible path for sensitive financial data to flow into LlamaFactory prompts or training inputs if bridged externally.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal outputs financial or licensed data into prompts consumed by LlamaFactory, leakage occurs.
IF an operator exports OpenBBTerminal results into LlamaFactory training data, the data class is propagated.
mitigations: Do not feed OpenBBTerminal outputs into LlamaFactory without redaction.
Restrict OpenBBTerminal API access to trusted localhost clients only.
Review prompts for financial or licensed data before reuse.
requires-engineering: implement data-class filters on any export path.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git state, or use MCP, so it has little direct write overlap with OpenBBTerminal. OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and multiple instances, but the profiles do not show shared writable resources or locking issues. The main conflict risk is limited to external orchestration, not default agent behavior.
conditions: IF both agents are attached to the same mutable external resource through an orchestrator, write conflicts become possible.
IF OpenBBTerminal is run with shared MCP state across instances, coordination issues can appear.
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate workspace.
Avoid sharing git repositories or writable directories between them.
Limit OpenBBTerminal to one active instance per resource.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable backend.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can emit API/MCP results that a downstream system may treat as authoritative, while LlamaFactory is a model-training/fine-tuning tool that could propagate those outputs into prompts or datasets. The profiles do not document verification gates between them, so a mistaken OpenBBTerminal output could cascade into LlamaFactory-generated artifacts.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal outputs are reused as training or prompt data without review, errors can cascade.
IF an operator treats OpenBBTerminal results as ground truth, downstream artifacts may inherit mistakes.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before reuse of OpenBBTerminal outputs.
Label OpenBBTerminal outputs as untrusted data in downstream prompts.
Keep training corpora separate from live market outputs.
requires-engineering: add automated validation against source data.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, which can carry retention, licensing, and residency obligations, while LlamaFactory is an open-source fine-tuning tool with no compliance controls documented here. Because the pair lacks documented retention or residency alignment, compliance mismatch is plausible even though no specific jurisdiction is stated.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data is routed from OpenBBTerminal into LlamaFactory workflows, compliance obligations may be violated.
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to the shared data class, the pair lacks documented controls.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data into LlamaFactory workflows.
Confirm licensing terms before exporting OpenBBTerminal data.
Document retention and deletion handling for any shared dataset.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
